problems.problem: The contact detail (crop 62,1069,585,1319) proves the bottle base touches the limestone at y=1209 with a real soft contact shadow (spec offset_y 0 is correct, do not move it), but that shadow is a neutral ambient pool while the background shows a hard raking sun edge at the upper left and the product cutout carries soft frontal-top studio speculars. Three different light stories coexist: the bottle reads pasted onto the wall/ground junction instead of standing in the declared sunlight.

The 'honed limestone ground' rendered as glossy veined marble tiles with visible grout lines andSheen, contradicting the declared matte honed limestone and the matte mineral grain of the wall; the tiled foreground fights the ultramarine plaster and cheapens the courtyard concept.

The promised single crisp diagonal shadow edge is only a small dark wedge clipped at the top-left canvas corner; most of the wall is flat unmodulated ultramarine, so the sundial concept reads as an accident at the frame edge rather than as composed light.

Hierarchy inside the right column is top-loaded and then collapses: after the strong two-line title there is a ~110 px void before 'EAU DE PARFUM' (y 907) and the gold rule (y 976), leaving the lower third of the column and the area beside the bottle body empty; the column does not visually close against the bottle base line.

The bottle occupies the left 47% but its base sits exactly on the wall/ground junction line, so the foreground floor band (y 1210-1440) is dead space holding nothing; references (Hermes, Sisley) let the ground plane carry shadow and props, here it is an empty tiled strip that disconnects product from setting.

changes.value: Deep ultramarine lime-washed plaster wall meeting a continuous matte honed pale limestone ground with no tiles and no grout lines, one broad hard diagonal shadow edge raking the wall from upper left across a third of its height, bright warm direct sunlight grazing the mineral grain, empty scene, no objects
